unreg:half_full_double_result.blueprint_mechanism: Half and quarter markets inherit the game-level strength model with period-specific structure: scripted openers and opening-possession order, first-half vs second-half style (starters in/out, blowout management), halftime adjustments and end-of-half drives. Period scores are smaller and lumpier so ties and zero scoring have material mass; spreads on halves use margin distributions at period end.

unreg:half_full_double_result.target: Probability of a stated (1st-half result, full-game result) pair, half ties allowed, full game incl. OT.
unreg:half_full_double_result.why_distinct: Settles on the joint of first-half and full-game margins; needs their dependence (comebacks, half ties), which a marginal half-side or full-game moneyline model does not produce.

blueprint_inputs.why: Market-implied strength anchors the prior and absorbs sharp information.
Composite ratings give an independent strength estimate and benchmark.
Opponent-adjusted offense efficiency drives scoring margin.
Opponent-adjusted defense efficiency completes the margin estimate.
Conference-level offsets prevent weak-schedule inflation in adjusted stats.
QB identity at decision time shifts margin by points.
Availability news (sparse) changes strength late.
Home-field effects vary widely; neutral sites remove them.
Short weeks, byes and travel create small effects.
Rivalry, bowl, playoff stakes and opt-outs.
Favorite behavior with large leads changes cover probabilities for big spreads.
Fat-tailed margin residuals and key numbers.
Overtime has no ties but extends the game; wording matters.
Sharp reference lines for benchmarking.
Regulation vs OT inclusion and period definitions.
Roster churn from the portal makes last season's results a weaker guide, especially early in the season.
Quote history shows how fast the market absorbs QB news.

unreg:multi_leg_parlay_packs.blueprint_mechanism: College moneyline, spread and half/quarter side markets price the distribution of margin: opponent-adjusted team strength (efficiency, talent, QB), venue and travel, schedule spots and motivation shift the mean, while tails are fatter than in the NFL because of mismatches, blowout management and variable pace. Roster churn from the portal, no reliable injury feed and cross-conference connectivity make priors and calibration central.

unreg:multi_leg_parlay_packs.target: Probability that every leg of a pre-packaged combination resolves YES jointly: several named teams all win their games, or a spread cover and a total side in the same game both hit.
unreg:multi_leg_parlay_packs.why_distinct: Single-game archetypes price one marginal outcome; these settle on a conjunction of legs, so the target is a joint probability that needs the dependence structure between legs (near-independent across games, strongly correlated margin/total within a game), which no existing archetype models.

blueprint_inputs.why: Simulation of conference race and tiebreakers.
Format and seeding rules in force.
Time-varying market-implied strength with uncertainty is the base for simulations and futures prices.
Composite ratings provide an independent strength estimate and a check against the market-implied rating.
Preseason regression and returning production.
Forward-looking opponent strength over an unbalanced schedule drives expected wins and tiebreaker paths.
Lucky one-score records inflate rankings and perceived strength and regress going forward.
Ranking dynamics and committee behavior.
QB injury or change is the dominant single risk for a contender's season distribution.
Constraints across linked markets.
Sportsbook futures give benchmark probabilities after de-vig, though vig-heavy and sparse for small outcomes.
Contract defines eligibility, cancelled-game handling and which ranking or source resolves the market.

unreg:season_stat_leader.blueprint_mechanism: Season-level college outcomes (conference title, playoff berth, rankings, awards, national title) derive from team strength with uncertainty, the unbalanced schedule, tiebreakers and a selection process (committee/format) that adds non-statistical judgement; format changes and conference realignment change structure; roster churn and QB injuries dominate preseason uncertainty.

KXNCAAFACCLEADER.rules_secondary:
All regular season games count towards this market, regardless of whether the game is within conference. Conference championship games are not included in the regular season. 
If Lincoln Kienholz does not play in the ACC in the 2026 regular season for any reason, the market for that player resolves to No.
If multiple players are tied for the most passing touchdowns at the end of the regular season, “Yes” positions will pay $1/N (rounded down to the nearest cent), where N is the number of tied players, and “No” positions will pay 1 minus the "Yes" payout.
